question: to the Commission Emma Rafowicz (S&D), Joanna Scheuring-Wielgus (S&D) Subject:

The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger will create an entity with strong market positions in film production, distribution and streaming. This may lead to price increases, pressure on theatrical exclusivity windows and a reduction in the number and diversity of films released, with implications for audience choice and cultural diversity. The merger may affect European independent producers and creators through fewer commissioning editors and reduced access to financing and distribution, undermining film diversity for European audiences and the viability of Europe’s creative industries. Based on the above: 1.

How will the Commission assess the merger’s impact on competition in the EU’s audiovisual sector, particularly regarding market concentration, the number and diversity of films released, and bargaining power vis-à-vis cinemas and independent producers?
Does the Commission intend to request the opinion of the European Board for Media Services under Article 23 of the European Media Freedom Act?

Will the Commission ensure that the parties offer commitments to address the risks of worsening commercial terms, reduced theatrical exclusivity, loss of cultural diversity and reduced sustainability of the European film ecosystem and does it consider that, if adequate remedies cannot be secured, the merger should be blocked?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.8.2026) On 22 July 2026, the proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance Corporation was approved by the Commission subject to conditions. The Commission thoroughly assessed the impact of the proposed acquisition in the EU from all possible angles, including but not limited to: (i) the production of films for cinema release, (ii) the distribution of films for cinema release; (iii) the distribution of television channels and (iv) streaming services. The assessment revealed that the concentration would lead to competition concerns in the European Economic Area (EEA) countries where Paramount currently distributes films to cinemas under the joint venture United International Pictures (‘UIP’) with Universal. Therefore, the Commission accepted remedy measures proposed by the parties that ensure the termination of Paramount’s stake in UIP in the EEA. The primary way for the European Board for Media Services (the Board) to draw up its opinions concerning media market concentrations is under Article 22 of the European Media Freedom Act (EMFA)1, where a media market concentration is likely to affect the functioning of the internal market for media services and upon consultation by the national regulatory authority or body concerned. Drawing up an opinion under Article 23 of the EMFA is conditional on the absence of an assessment or a consultation by the national regulatory authority or body concerned. At this stage, the Commission does not intend to request the opinion of the Board under Article 23 of the EMFA. In the event that the Commission’s assessment under the EU Merger Regulation does not align with a future opinion of the Board or any national media authority, the Commission’s assessment is without prejudice to the assessment that is carried out by the relevant media authorities.2
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1083 of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a common framework
for media services in the internal market and amending Directive 2010/13/EU (European Media Freedom Act), OJ L 2024/1083, 17.4.2024, p. 1. 2 Article 22(1) EMFA.
